Disseqt AI raises $8 Mn led by Gresham House Ventures, Rahul Dravid joins round
AI governance and assurance startup Disseqt AI has raised $8 million in a funding round led by Gresham House Ventures, with participation from existing investor Sure Valley Ventures (SVV), Delta Partners and Enterprise Ireland.
Gyan Vardhan
19 Nov 2026
13:56
IST
Follow Us
New Update
AI governance and assurance startup Disseqt AI has raised $8 million in pre-Series A funding round led by Gresham House Ventures, with participation from existing investor Sure Valley Ventures (SVV), Delta Partners and Enterprise Ireland.
The round also saw participation from angel investors, including senior executives from OpenAI, Palo Alto Networks, Salesforce and Meta, along with former Indian cricket captain Rahul Dravid, who invested in his individual capacity.
The fresh funds will be utilized to expand its enterprise customer base globally and hiring across sales, operations and technology roles in India, Disseqt said in a press release.
Founded in late 2025 by Apoorva Kumar, Manish Atri and Cyril Treacy, Disseqt AI provides an AI governance and assurance platform that helps enterprises test, monitor and govern AI applications and agents.
Its platform enables businesses to assess AI agents for vulnerabilities before deployment, enforce company policies once they go live, and continuously monitor their behaviour. It can also block outputs that violate organisational policies while maintaining audit trails for compliance and oversight.
The platform allows enterprises to test whether AI agents can be manipulated into revealing confidential customer information or exhibiting other vulnerabilities before being deployed in business operations.
The funding comes amid growing enterprise adoption of AI agents and increasing concerns around their safety, security and regulatory compliance. According to McKinsey's 2026 State of AI survey, 40% of respondents at companies with annual revenues exceeding $1 billion were scaling AI agents in at least one business function, compared with 27% a year earlier.
Disseqt said it has already deployed its assurance capabilities across multiple enterprise use cases. In a project involving a global sports league's fan engagement agent, which serves 80 million fans, the company improved the safe-response rate from 80% to 99% across tests covering safety, bias and privacy risks. It added that no unsafe outputs were detected when the original failing tests were repeated after fixes.
The company also provides assurance services for a credit card services programme at a large European bank.
The investment marks another bet on the emerging AI governance and assurance segment, as enterprises look to deploy autonomous AI systems across customer interactions, financial services and internal business operations.

Bengaluru accounts for 36 per cent of funding raised by India's AI startups
Bengaluru-based startups have raised around $85 billion since 2010, accounting for 47% of the total venture funding raised by Indian startups.
Karnataka Minister for Electronics, Information Technology (IT), Biotechnology (BT), and e-Governance Priyank Kharge (File Photo | ANI)
Express News Service
Updated on :
19 Nov 2026, 6:07 am
2 min read
Copied
BENGALURU: Bengaluru accounts for 36.3% of the funding raised by native artificial intelligence (AI) startups in India and is home to 71% of the country's AI and deep-tech unicorns created since 2023, according to the Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026, released by IT and BT Minister Priyank Kharge at the Bengaluru Tech Summit on Wednesday.
Prepared by the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission (KDEM), the report highlights Bengaluru's position in India's startup ecosystem, covering funding, deep tech, AI, unicorns, women entrepreneurs, IPOs and emerging technology hubs across Karnataka.
Presenting the report, Siddarth Pai, founding partner of 3one4 Capital, said Karnataka's digital economy was valued at $159 billion and was projected to reach nearly $400 billion by 2031-32. The state accounted for 47% of India's venture capital funding between 2016 and 2026, amounting to $85 billion, the report said.
Of the 1,556 deep-tech startups founded in Bengaluru since 2010, 1,319 are active and funded, having raised a total of $3.77 billion. The city also has 799 native AI startups, of which 764 are active and funded.
Bengaluru-based startups have raised around $85 billion since 2010, accounting for 47% of the total venture funding raised by Indian startups. Of this, $76.5 billion was raised in the past decade. The city has 3,810 active, funded startups founded since 2010, nearly twice Mumbai's 1,982.
The report puts the combined valuation of Bengaluru's 57 unicorns at $211 billion. They account for 44% of India's 131 unicorns and 55.3% of their combined valuation. Bengaluru has produced 46 of India's 100 unicorns since 2020, with startups taking an average of six years to attain unicorn status.
The city also has 212 soonicorns, accounting for 36% of India's total of 589, ahead of Delhi NCR (134) and Mumbai (121). Bengaluru startups take around five years to reach soonicorn status.
Nearly 30% of India's active, funded women-led deep-tech and native AI startups were founded in Bengaluru. These companies have collectively raised $323.65 million, the report said.
Bengaluru also accounts for a significant share of startup listings. Sixteen companies linked to the city have been listed since November 2024, with a combined valuation of around $42 billion at the time of listing. Bengaluru accounts for 33 of the 226 IPOs by funded companies in India during this period, while Karnataka-headquartered companies account for 37, or around 16%.
Startups in Bengaluru take an average of 8.2 years from founding to exit, compared with the global average of 11.1 years. Karnataka has around 300 venture capital firms, while Bengaluru is home to 75 Category I Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), accounting for 21% of India's total and ranking second after Mumbai.

The company will use the capital to develop new artificial intelligence capabilities for its physical AI platform, SyncOS, improve the performance of its autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), and expand its engineering and project delivery teams in India. It also plans to deepen partnerships with local systems integrators and automation providers.
Founded in 2019 by Rahul Nambiar, Nikhil Venkatesh and Prashant Trivedi, Botsync combines autonomous mobile robots with SyncOS, a software platform that connects robots, machines and enterprise systems within a manufacturing facility. The system coordinates workflows and material movement across production floors and warehouses, allowing different automation systems to operate through a common interface.
The company’s platform also analyses operational data to identify bottlenecks, predict maintenance requirements and improve throughput.
Botsync has completed more than 70 projects across six countries, executing over two million production tasks at 99 per cent uptime, according to the company. It says customers have been able to recover their investments within 24 months through reduced dependence on forklifts and manual material handling, alongside improvements in productivity. Its global customers include Caterpillar, Ford, Nestle, Honda, Coca-Cola and Kimberly-Clark.
The company is also looking to expand its presence in Australia and establish a go-to-market operation in the US, while continuing to serve Singapore, India, Thailand and Indonesia. Its expansion plans include building a wider network of robot manufacturers and providers of factory and warehouse software that can integrate with SyncOS.

Vietnamese AI-powered used car startup Vucar secures fresh funding
Copy link
19/11/2026 09:29 (GMT+07:00)
Founded by entrepreneurs born in 1999, Vietnamese startup Vucar has secured another multimillion-dollar investment to expand its AI-powered used car valuation and online auction platform.
Vietnamese technology startup Vucar has completed a Pre-Series A funding round led by OSK-SBI Venture Partners, with existing investors Monk's Hill Ventures of Singapore and Antler also participating.
Founded in Ho Chi Minh City in 2023 by a group of entrepreneurs born in 1999, Vucar operates a platform combining artificial intelligence (AI), on-site vehicle inspections and online auctions to simplify used car transactions.
The company did not disclose the exact funding amount, but a representative said the investment could reach several million US dollars.
Vucar previously raised a million-dollar seed funding round in September 2024. The latest investment signals continued international investor interest in its business model and expansion potential in Vietnam's used car market.
AI-powered valuations based on over 4 million data points
Vucar's founders, all born in 1999, have secured another multimillion-dollar funding round for their used car trading platform. Photo: Vucar
Determining a fair selling price remains one of the biggest challenges in Vietnam's used car market.
Even vehicles of the same model, production year and variant can command significantly different prices depending on mileage, engine condition, bodywork, maintenance history and market demand.
Overpricing can leave a vehicle unsold for an extended period, while undervaluing it can result in financial losses for the owner. Buyers also face difficulties assessing whether asking prices accurately reflect a vehicle's condition.
Vucar has developed an AI-powered valuation tool using more than 4 million data points to generate indicative prices based on each vehicle's characteristics and condition.
Rather than relying solely on advertised prices across online marketplaces, the system aims to provide faster market insights and help owners estimate their vehicles' value before deciding to sell.
The startup has also introduced an AI assistant that answers questions from buyers and sellers about individual vehicles, reducing response times and easing the workload of customer service staff.
However, Vucar does not rely entirely on algorithms.
Physical inspections, document verification, contract assistance and vehicle handovers remain the responsibility of its employees.
"AI helps us value cars faster and respond to customers almost instantly. But no algorithm can replace someone who visits the vehicle in person and supports the customer until payment is received. Car sellers need both," said Jake Vu, CEO and co-founder of Vucar.
The company's sales process is designed to minimize the tasks owners must handle themselves.
Sellers submit their vehicle information through Vucar's website, after which a company specialist conducts a free on-site inspection.
